#3418. Apple staff accused of signing up customers to subscriptions without consent; company responds

Repair technician turned consumer rights advocate Louis Rossmann recently accused Apple store staff of signing up customers to the company’s services subscriptions without their consent.

Apple has not yet commented, but has taken two steps indicating that the company takes the accusations seriously …

Rossmann is a repair technician who specializes in component-level logic board repairs and data recovery. He later became a key figure in advocating for right-to-repair legislation, which Apple initially opposed and later backed.

In a recent video, he claimed that some Apple store staff were signing up customers to trials of paid services subscriptions without their informed consent. Targets set by Apple are said to have encouraged the practice.

Customers accepting the offer of a personalized shopping experience could be shown the free trials of Apple services available to them based on their recent purchases. For example, buying an iPhone currently entitles you to a free three-month subscription to Apple TV. However, these trials automatically start debiting your payment method if you don’t cancel them before they end.

Staff were instructed to show these offers to customers and were allegedly set a 40% sign-up target, which Apple tracked as a performance metric. Crucially, the offers are shown on the employee’s device rather than on the customer’s phone. A store member told Rossman that some staff were hitting the Accept button without properly obtaining consent from customers in order to hit their target.

When I asked whether they’d seen a specialist press Agree with their own eyes, they answered “Yes, I saw some specialists press on behalf of the customer. So, they are hitting agree. They are signing the customer up to something without actually having the customer click okay, hit okay, or provide express consent.”

The store member also claimed that staff were describing the offer as a gift, which further disguised the fact that it would turn into a paid recurring subscription unless canceled.

This is not shocking to me. Apple started pushing subscriptions during the sales process years ago when I worked in the stores.

I remember this being a major shift from being more customer focused over to becoming a battleground of a sales floor trying to get your "numbers". I even recall hearing that someone got promoted because their numbers were "so good" while we all knew they were signing people for AC+ without their knowledge. Sad days.

At the time of writing, Apple has not responded directly to the accusations, but in a follow-up video yesterday Rossman cites a staff member describing the company’s response.

He says a memo was read out in the morning meeting stating that only customers could press the Accept button, and internal systems indicate Apple is no longer grading staff on the signup metric.

We have reached out to Apple for comment and will update with any response.

I live in one of the most densely populated states in the country, but even with New Jersey’s small size, there are still dead zones lurking around. Google Fi is tackling this persistent problem in 2026 with the rollout of its new "super network," which is designed to automatically switch between two 5G cellular networks in real time.

Google Fi’s "super network" switching is powered by Multiple Enabled Profiles (MEP) eSIM technology, which essentially allows a single physical eSIM to run two carrier profiles at the same time. Instead of treating the second connection as an inactive backup, the phone maintains active links to two separate cellular 5G networks. Therefore, if the signal degrades — whether due to congestion, tower interference, or physical obstacles — Google Fi's software automatically switches over to the secondary connection to prevent dropouts. It directly tackles the dead zones that cause reels to buffer or download speeds to crater.

While Google’s announcement doesn’t explicitly name which carriers it's partnering with to pull this off — choosing instead to label them simply as "two of America's fastest 5G networks" — there are plenty of clues. T-Mobile remains Google Fi’s primary host carrier, while the secondary partner providing the dual-coverage failover is described in as a "major carrier," defined as an "MNO or MVNO with more than 1 million customers in the U.S. as of March 2025."

Even the strongest cellular signal can struggle inside crowded spaces like airport terminals, shopping malls, and dense high-rises. That’s where Wi-Fi Auto-Connect+ steps in to supplement coverage by automatically identifying and linking your phone to high-quality public Wi-Fi networks. It does this without requiring manual logins, portal verifications, or toggling Wi-Fi menus, keeping the handoff completely seamless.

Google Fi is carrying the super network abroad as well, enabling real-time network switching and Wi-Fi Auto-Connect+ across international travel destinations. By pairing dual-carrier 5G failover on the road with automated Wi-Fi in crowded venues, Google Fi makes staying reliably connected practically effortless no matter where you travel.

#3415. Teens and parents can expect Instagram notifications about AI age estimation

Meta says it’s expanding its AI age estimation globally to automatically extend Instagram account protections to millions more teenagers. It says parents in the US can also expect to receive notifications later this month …

Instagram has a number of protections for the accounts of teenagers, but it’s very common for teens to lie about their age in order to circumvent them. Back in May, the company said it would be using AI-powered age estimation to address the problem.

The company said it would use the tool to block users aged below 13, and to ensure that those in the 13 to 17 range had limited accounts. Teen accounts have age-appropriate feeds, limitations on who can interact with them, and default time management tools – though things didn’t get off to the best of starts when a 12-year-old kid fooled it by using an eyebrow pencil to draw a fake moustache.

Meta today says that it is rolling out the (hopefully now eyebrow pencil-proof) tech globally.

We use AI technology to find people we suspect to be teens, even if they use an adult birthday, and place them in Teen Account protections. Since first introducing this technology, we’ve been placing more teens in age-appropriate protections and are encouraged by the results. Based on that success, today we’re expanding this technology globally.

The company goes on to say that parents in the US will receive a notification sometime this month, with a link to a video and an article about the system.

This month, parents in the United States will begin to see an in-feed video on Instagram explaining our approach to ensuring their teens are in age-appropriate protections. The video will link to an article, written by Larry Magid, internet safety advocate and President and CEO of ConnectSafely, detailing our multi-layered age assurance approach, which includes keeping children under 13 off our platforms, providing age appropriate experiences for teens, and informing parents about ways they can partner with us to ensure their teens provide the correct age online.

If you don’t want to wait, you can read the article here.

Meta says the same protections will be rolled out to Threads and Facebook, although I would have thought being on Facebook in the first place is proof that it’s been a while since you were a teenager …

#3414. All 8 Episodes of 'VisionQuest,' Ranked

Spoiler Alert: This list contains spoilers for the VisionQuest finale.With VisionQuest finally finishing up its limited series run, Marvel fans are extremely happy. The finale to the trilogy that began with WandaVision is making its rounds as a fan-favorite Disney+ series. This is all thanks to the fact that the show has all the makings of a good superhero television series, while still staying extremely true to itself.

The character of Vision (Paul Bettany) has been through the ringer since his birth in Avengers: Age of Ultron, and while many had thought his story ended with his death in Avengers: Infinity War, the likes of WandaVision revived him (in a way). While, at first, there were lots of people who weren't happy about this new Vision being introduced, VisionQuest's eight awesome episodes have given them ample reason to be.

VisionQuest Episode 5, "Firewall" is a bit more of a sit-down-and-breathe episode, so it takes itself a tad slower than the rest of the others. This doesn't mean it's any kind of snooze-fest, though. Episode 5 is a lot more character-driven, especially when it comes to the likes of antagonists Jocasta (T'Nia Miller) and Ultron (James Spader). This fifth entry does quite a bit of legwork to make them more understandable as characters moving into the latter half of the season.

Having good, relatable, and sympathetic characters as antagonists is wildly important, and the Marvel Cinematic Universe can either be really good at this, or quite bad. Episode 5 makes it so VisionQuest truly succeeds on the antagonist front (even though the true villain of the series had yet to be truly introduced). It's not a perfect episode, and sometimes the pacing really keeps it from being everything it could be. But, all-in-all, it's still a decent episode that develops the characters effectively.

The first few episodes of a new show are extremely important. If the audiences are hooked by the first or second episode, the crew behind the series needs to make sure that hook stays and that was the important job that VisionQuest Episode 3, "Reboot" had. Thankfully, things are really kicking into high gear by this point in the plot, with Tommy Shepherd/Maximoff (Ruaridh Mollica) and Vision finally paired up and working together in full force.

The third entry also further develops the mystery behind whom the so-called "Butcherbird" is, and why they have been killing so specifically. This mystery truly engages viewers and keeps them guessing. This, combined with the great character work written between Tommy and Vision, makes Episode 3 a great continuation to the borderline perfect introduction that was in the first two episodes (which dropped together).

A good pilot for a television show is everything. If a pilot fails, the potential continued viewership of the show drops drastically. While the MCU has pre-installed fans that will watch whatever they put out, a bad pilot can still crash the plane and detract even the most dedicated viewer. Thankfully, director Christopher J. Byrne did a wonderful job bringing this new story to viewers.

Byrne reintroduces the audience to Vision and where he's been in the time since WandaVision with prowess and grace. Not to mention, it wastes no time introducing all the main players and the conflict. This faster pacing doesn't keep it from feeling too fast, though, and it still takes ample time to slow down and establish these characters, where they're at in their journeys, and what's to come. VisionQuest Episode 1, "No Strings" is a great example of an effective beginning.

The truth of Tommy's past is a mystery (to him) that lingers over his entire character arc. That presence is very prominent in VisionQuest Episode 6, "Deadlock" as they head to Madripoor to meet with Paladin (Todd Stashwick) for a tense alliance. If it isn't obvious from online discussion, the son of Vision is a fan-favorite character in the series, and this is a big episode for his character arc.

VisionQuest does a great job making reveals while still maintaining as much mystery as they can, and it doesn't just do that with Tommy's past in the sixth installment, but regarding the mysterious man behind all the shenanigans thus far. Not to mention, it's got a wonderful MCU callback cameo in Faran Tahir returning as Raza for the first time since Iron Man in 2008. A super fun inclusion that awards MCU fans who have been here since the beginning and still made it this far into such an expansive universe.

Four villains, and four arguments the films were honest enough to actually let them make. Here is the one you lean towards, the part of it that holds up, and the exact point where it stops holding up.

You align with the one who was right about the problem and wrong about the solution. Killmonger is the most persuasive villain Marvel has produced because the film never pretends his anger came from nowhere.

You align with the protector, which is the most understandable and most dangerous position on this list. Namor is not chasing power or revenge, he is doing whatever keeps his people hidden, and he has been doing it for centuries.

You align with the patient one, the only man on this list with no powers, no army and no hurry. Zemo lost his family in Sokovia and then spent years working out that you do not fight the Avengers, you introduce them to each other's secrets.

You align with the one who decided the answer was arithmetic. Thanos is not angry and not grieving in any way he will admit to, he simply reached a conclusion and never once revisited it, which is precisely what makes him frightening.

Just as a good pilot is important, a good finale is just as important—if not more so. VisionQuest had a lot it needed to accomplish by the end of the runtime of VisionQuest Episode 8, "Forever" and, thankfully, it managed to execute on it. MCU Disney+ finales have definitely struggled in the past, so this story had a lot to prove, with high stakes. There was a lot to be screwed up here, and, if everyone on the team—cast and crew alike—didn't give their A game, it could have turned out catastrophically. A bad finale can tarnish how people view a series as a whole forever, unfortunately.

The show's first seven episodes are incredibly strong, so to fumble in the final hour would have been horrific for the show's reputation and overall quality. "Forever" wraps up every plot thread relatively well, being able to weave the plots together into one cohesively. Everyone's character arcs feel like they've reached a natural conclusion, and the way that Vision finally bests Ultron is quite creative, as it doesn't rely on just action to wrap the conflict up. Plus, it gets huge points for finally bringing the Maximoff boys together, with Billy Maximoff (Joe Locke) making an appearance to help Tommy revive their father.

VisionQuest Episode 1, "No Strings" focuses mainly on introducing Vision and his AI crew, but they're not the only protagonists of this show. On the other hand, VisionQuest Episode 2, "Theseus", takes its entire runtime to introduce the character of Tommy and develop his side of this world and his character arc. Ever since WandaVision and Agatha All Along, people have been wondering where he's at. Is he alive? Where did he end up? What does he even look like?

This second episode answers all those questions. So, in a way, this is a bit of a "second pilot"—a job that it wonderfully succeeds at. The young man was always going to be one of the most important characters of this show, so giving him an entire episode to be introduced and established was an incredible call on the VisionQuest team's part. This is especially true with the great direction, as per usual, from Christopher J. Byrne.

Comic book fans were abundantly excited when it was announced that the awesome villain, Jocasta, was going to be making her MCU debut in VisionQuest. If there's an episode to consider the "Jocasta Episode," it would be VisionQuest Episode 4, "Malware" as it's her big introduction and the reveal of her major plans for the future. This episode also throws a bit of a wrench in the father and son's relationship, as the young speedster discovers that Vision wasn't wholly honest about who resides in his mind.

With Tommy putting it together that Ultron is in Vision's mind, he's obviously not very happy with his father. Things get worse, however, when Jocasta makes her move, and Vision is forced into letting Ultron take control to stop her—which, to no one's surprise, does not go well. Tommy also gets to finally show off his true speed in the climax of this episode, which is abundantly cool to finally see on display.

A good penultimate episode needs to tee up what's to come in the big finale, and—genuinely—VisionQuest Episode 7, "Immolation" is one of the best penultimate Disney+ MCU episodes of all time. The way this seventh episode sets up what's to come and reveals such massive information to the audience is masterful in every way. It truly puts Vision and Ultron at odds, brings Jocasta one step closer to her goal, sets Tommy up for a huge arc conclusion, and so much more.

VisionQuest Episode 7, "Immolation" has everything that makes this show as great as it is. It has some of the most raw, vulnerable dialogue and character moments out there that bring these characters to where they need to be perfectly. It's got action that ups the ante with spectacle and wonder. Not to mention, the visuals continue to be astounding, thanks to Director of Photography, Neville Kidd. With this in mind, there's just no question that the penultimate entry to the VisionQuest journey is the best the show has to offer. The stakes are set, the characters are ready, and the crew executed everything they needed to with so much prowess.

#3413. Apple Won't Make a Small Phone so This Company Is Stepping In

Big smartphones have long been the norm. It seems many, if not most, of us prefer our smartphones to be akin to tiny tablets. Even Apple's smallest iPhone isn't that small, with a 6.1-inch display. (Compare that to the 5.4-inch iPhone mini it used to sell.) But just because a lot of us like it that way doesn't mean all of us do.

Despite what companies like Apple would lead you to believe, there are plenty of people out there who want their smartphones to be smaller. For some, the iPhone mini was perfect, featuring a design that most could use comfortably with one hand. While the sales might not have been steady enough for Apple to continue producing the mini line, anecdotally, I know quite a few people who would happily keep using iPhones this small, if only Apple would make more of them. Perhaps you know people like this too; maybe you're one of them.

While the rumor mill does not suggest that Apple plans to make a new iPhone mini, that doesn't mean the dream of the tiny smartphone is dead. Enter "Enough Phone," a new device with a humble goal: to create a "small, modern smartphone that's enough."

Enough Phone really does seem small. The company says its upcoming device is 133mm by 64mm, and less than 12mm thick. That's the equivalent of 5.24 inches by 2.52 inches, and less than 0.47 inches thick. It's remarkably similar to the iPhone 13 mini, at 5.18 by 2.53 inches, and 0.3 inches thick. While the Enough Phone might be a tad larger overall, and perhaps noticeably thicker, it's still reminiscent of that "mini" footprint.

The Enough Phone's 5.3-inch display isn't particularly modern, however. While we don't know the display type, we do know that it has a resolution of 1520 x 720, which may look less sharp to anyone coming from the 2340 x 1080 resolution of the iPhone 13 mini. I'd wager that most people interested in a device like this aren't looking for an ultra-sharp OLED display anyway, but it's worth noting here.

As for the Enough Phone's other specs, the company says it plans to pack in a 2.4GHz MediaTek Dimensity 7500 chip with 8GB of RAM, 128GB of built-in storage, though you can expand that with a microSD card (something you don't see on many smartphones these days). The current plan is to ship with a single 50MP Sony IMX766 rear camera, and a 32MP selfie cam, which would be amongst the highest-resolution front-facing cameras on any smartphone. It supports 5G, Wi-Fi 6, and eSIM, with the option to use a physical SIM as well.

Enough is also aiming to make its smartphone more repairable than the competition. While smartphone OEMs have made slight improvements to repairability in recent years, few phones are made to be opened up by the user, and their components replaced. While Enough Phone isn't fully modular, it is designed with easy-to-open screws, and comes with a fully replaceable 3,500 mAh battery. Combined with promised software support through 2032, Enough says this device "should last you into the next decade."

Now, all of these specs are targets, as the phone is currently in the prototype stage. Enough says that final details may change "slightly" during testing. I would at least hope that the dimensions, particularly the screen size, remain the same by launch. What will likely stay the same, however, are the ringtones: Enough says they hired composer Brian Squillance of LAANDS to produce the jingles for its phone, which is a neat touch.

Unfortunately for Apple fans, however, Enough Phone isn't an iPhone. That said, it doesn't have to be an Android phone, either. While you can buy the phone with Android 17 installed, you can also choose to run OdysseyOS, a minimalist "de-Googled" operating system made by SLEKE. Enough says OdysseyOS is meant for "intentional phone use," which might appeal to anyone looking for a phone that's "dumb" as well as small.

Of course, neither operating system is iOS. Unfortunately for Apple users, the only true iPhone options here are to continue using an old iPhone mini, which Apple does still support, or to opt for an iPhone 17e, the smallest iPhone the company currently makes. It's pretty easy to find a used and refurbished iPhone 13 mini for reasonable price; but while they can still run the latest version of iOS, you won't be able to take advantage of all of Apple's newest features. Plus, while there's no telling how long Apple plans to support the 13 line for, it won't support it forever—by iOS 28 or iOS 29, your phone might lose support entirely.

If the promise of a modern mini smartphone entices you, you can back the Enough Phone on Kickstarter today. While the company's $399 "Super Early Bird" reward is already sold out, as of this article, the "Early Bird" reward is still up. That reward costs $449, and includes a glass screen protector pre-installed, a protective case, a USB-C cable, a USB-C to 3.5mm headphone adapter, a hex screwdriver, and green "Founders' Edition" backplate screws. Enough says that the retail price for its phone will be $599 after the campaign, so you can save $150 by backing the phone today—if you're serious about small phones. The Enough Phone is slated for a May 2027 launch.

Based on those MCU post-credits scenes, Doctor Doom is clearly assembling a powerful team of his own, either through mind-control or by taking the powers of some of the Marvel Studios franchise's most powerful characters, a category both the Hulk and Wanda fall into. There is a factor that boosts the mind-control theories, as that is an ability the Scarlet Witch has famously mastered through magic, which Downey's Victor von Doom could also know how to wield, given he managed to resurrect Wanda. Additionally, there are mysterious Latverian witches in Avengers: Doomsday, with one of them wearing red robes, which could be a mind-controlled Wanda.

Avengers: Doomsday will feature several powerful Marvel characters, but looking at the upcoming MCU movie's trailers, Tom Hiddleston's Loki has not appeared in the footage nearly as much as the rest. That, added to the fact that Loki is right on Doom's path to reshape the multiverse, given how the God of Stories' role is to protect the multiversal branches of Yggdrasil, positions Hiddleston's character as a fitting addition to the villain's growing list of kidnapped heroes.

Loki could also have a darker fate, as it would make more sense for Doctor Doom to kill him and take Loki's multiversal powers than to attempt a mind-control spell on him like the existence of the Latverian witches suggests might be the case for Wanda.

That said, it would also track if Doom was simply building his own team to fight the combined might of two Avengers squads, the Fantastic Four, and Fox's X-Men, as those superhero teams have powerful characters like Thor, Sentry, Magneto, and more. With few Avengers: Doomsday details revealed a month before the film's release, Marvel's new Scarlet Witch reveal, and its Hulk connection is an exciting update.

#3411. Apple pushing faster on agentic Siri would carry three big risks

Yesterday saw two reports about Apple software development. The first said that the company was aiming to give Siri more agentic capabilities “as soon as next year,” while the second said that CEO John Ternus is pushing Craig Federighi to speed up software development.

If accurate, it seems near-certain the two reports are connected. But if Ternus really is pushing for an acceleration in Siri’s ability to act as an AI agent, that comes with three potentially huge risks …

Both reports were by Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, though he didn’t directly connect them. On the Siri side, his newsletter contrasted the agentic abilities of some competitor models, suggesting that Apple ultimately wants to achieve the same things.

Dots, Muse and Grok can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step. Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I’m told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year.

The report about Ternus pushing Federighi for faster software development mentions “moving beyond necessary improvements to Siri,” of which agentic capabilities would be the obvious candidate.

But agentic capabilities are among the most dangerous forms of AI given the multitude of things that could go very, very wrong.

The most obvious is simply failing to carry out the task. Depending on the importance of it, the consequences could range from annoyance through to significant harm.

Technology has long failed to live up to one of its biggest promises: relieving us of mundane work in order to devote our time to more fulfilling things. For example, obtaining tickets to a popular gig or other event, which currently involves scheduling time in order to repeatedly refresh a page, perhaps wait through a queuing system, and finally carry out the transaction. It would be great to be able to hand this off to an AI.

But even on something relatively unimportant like this, if we delegated the task and the AI failed to obtain the tickets, especially if this was due to a silly error, this could prove enormously frustrating. If the task were more important, the results could obviously be far worse.

Potentially even worse is achieving the task but doing so in inappropriate ways. We’ve already seen high-profile examples of this, like the Hugging Face hack caused by an AI model seeking so hard to carry out instructions that it used underhand methods to bypass crucial safeguards in the process.

Over two thousand real secrets, including passwords, API tokens, SSH root logins, and even admin-level cloud keys, were found leaking on GitHub after developers clicked “Yes, and don’t ask again” in Claude Code […] When a developer grants Claude Code permission to proceed with “Yes, and don’t ask again,” it saves the exact command, including secrets, to a file, .claude/settings.local.json, inside the project folder. This file should never be exposed publicly [but] Apiiro, an application security company, found 104,185 public copies of such files on GitHub across 103,617 repositories.

This was just a few days after Anthropic started encouraging Claude users to connect their bank and finance card accounts to the AI chatbot. (My own answer is “Hell, no.”)

When we delegate a task to an AI system that requires access to any of our personal data, and we’re not expected to check on it again until the task is complete, the potential for disaster here is enormous.

It’s worth prefixing this with a note that the reliability of the paired reports is far from certain. In particular, in a closed-door meeting between Ternus and Federighi, it’s hard to see how the content could have leaked unless one of the two men chose to do this. If Ternus leaked it, that suggests a very high level of frustration on his part. But leaving that aside …

I hope Ternus is pushing Federighi for improved software quality and not just new features...

We’re currently witnessing an AI arms race, with each company aiming to beat its competitors to next-generation capabilities, even while acknowledging a non-trivial possibility that the pace of development could put humanity’s future at risk.

In my view, the very last thing we need is Apple joining this race. I know it can be frustrating when Apple lags behind other companies in the introduction of some types of new tech, but this is one field in which I would be very happy to see Apple proceed very much more cautiously than others.

What’s your view on this? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

#3407. 10 Great Thriller Movies Based on Best-Selling Books, Ranked

Novels remain one of the most significant sources of cinematic inspiration, and it takes a particular type of film to stay faithful to a story. From the bone-chilling adaptation of Thomas Harris' thriller, The Silence of the Lambs, to the intelligent and masterful novel by author Stieg Larsson's, The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo, there have been many successful adaptations of incredible books.

Popular novels turned into movies create an exciting opportunity for viewers to see the story play out visually, many of which have become some of the greatest thrillers ever to hit the big screen. While some thrillers remain loyal to the author's original novel, others carry the source material into previously unforeseen places. There have been many book-to-screen thriller adaptations, but certain ones stand out as cinematic masterpieces.

Children of Men is a dystopian action thriller that works on many levels, including as a cautionary story and a trailblazing human drama about society's struggle for survival. The film unfolds in 2027 London, where humanity is on the verge of extinction, and worldwide chaos ensues. When a woman falls pregnant, cynical bureaucrat Theo Faron (Clive Owen) and his ex-wife Julian Taylor (Julianne Moore) help secretly transport a pregnant refugee to safety. At the same time, they fight to protect the world's last remaining hope from danger.

Directed by Alfonso Cuarón and based on the 1992 novel The Children of Men by author P.D. James, the film received overwhelming critical acclaim but no box-office success. However, the powerful thriller has recently enjoyed a remarkable resurgence with glowing reappraisals on both sociopolitical and artistic grounds. The movie and novel contain general similarities, including a dystopian setting, developed main characters, and a strong plot that remains relevant with each passing year.

The psychological thriller The Girl on the Train follows divorced alcoholic Rachel Watson (Emily Blunt), who obsessively watches the house belonging to her ex-husband and his new wife on her morning train commute. Along the route, she catches glimpses of their neighbors, a seemingly perfect young couple, Scott and Megan. However, when Megan suddenly goes missing, Rachel is caught between helping to investigate the disappearance and becoming a murder suspect.

Directed by Tate Taylor and based on the bestselling novel by Paula Hawkins, the movie The Girl on the Train is an excellent example of a great mystery. The book-to-movie adaptation stays primarily loyal to its original material with only a few key changes, including the film's location switching from London to New York City and the original pair of detectives in the novel becoming one complicated character. The movie unfolds in diverse, compelling ways as it plays with the timeline and the narrator while keeping viewers guessing until the end.

In the movie The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo, disgraced journalist Mikael Blomkvist (Daniel Craig) hires brilliant computer hacker Lisbeth Salander (Rooney Mara) to help solve the 40-year-old murder of Henrik Vanger's (Christopher Plummer) niece. As the two main protagonists uncover the truth, they discover more than they bargained for about the powerful Vanger family secrets.

Masterfully directed by David Fincher and based on the novel by Swedish author Stieg Larsson, The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo film is a compelling psychological thriller. In the second book-to-movie adaptation, Fincher created a masterful neo-noir thriller that unravels a genuinely captivating story and remains faithful to the novel's intricate plot.

The erotic thriller Crash is one of director David Cronenberg's most controversial and provocative films. The movie follows film producer James Ballard (James Spader) and his wife Catherine (Deborah Kara Unger), who are looking to spice up their sex life. Following a car crash, they are lured into a strange subculture and underground community of sadomasochistic car-crash fetishists.

Cronenberg adapted J.G. Ballard's highly controversial future-shock novel into an immaculately directed, vivid depiction of graphic sexual acts instigated by violence. Both the movie and book present disturbing and equally profound inquiries into human desire. With its twisted and erotic portrayal of eroticism, this drama/thriller will grip its viewers entirely.

Set in New York City in the 1980s, American Psycho follows investment banker Patrick Bateman (Christian Bale), an egotistical psychopath consumed by the social politics of the upper-class circle. By nightfall, Bateman's corporate illusion drastically changes as his sadistic desires take full effect, shifting towards a double life as a serial killer.

Filmmaker Mary Harron's adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis' American Psycho is the epitome of cult cinema. While Ellis' novel is a satire of greed and heartlessness that consumed parts of America during the 1980s, Harron's film investigates similar themes but with the addition of dark humor. Both the novel and the film have polarized their audiences with horrifying brutality as they examine the elements that make a man a monster.

The psychological thriller Shutter Island follows troubled U.S. Marshall Edward "Teddy" Daniels (Leonardo DiCaprio) as he investigates the disappearance of a woman who has escaped an asylum for the criminally insane. As the investigation deepens, Daniels, while dealing with his haunting past, begins to realize things are not as they appear.

The film Shutter Island is arguably one of the most popular thrillers of all time and a haunting adaptation of Dennis Lehane's pulpy gothic novel. Director Martin Scorsese brilliantly uses visceral horror imagery to convey the despair of Daniel's tortured psyche. The psychological components detailed in both the book and movie continue to keep audiences guessing as to what is fact and what is fiction.

In the movie Gone Girl, New York-based writer Nick Dunne (Ben Affleck) and his wife Amy (Rosamund Pike) appear to be the perfect couple. However, when Amy suddenly disappears under suspicious circumstances, Nick becomes the prime suspect. The resulting media frenzy causes the couple's image of a blissful union to fade quickly, leading to compelling questions regarding who the real Nick and Amy.

Director David Fincher's adaptation of Gillian Flynn's Gone Girl resulted in a dark and intelligent psychological thriller, receiving widespread critical acclaim. While the film appears to be a straightforward mystery, it becomes much more complex with its jaw-dropping twists and turns. The book-to-film adaptation has successfully managed to remain faithful to the novel while also introducing its own creative style.

The movie Fight Club observes a depressed office worker (Edward Norton) and a soap salesman named Tyler Durden (Brad Pitt) forming an underground fight club. The club attracts other individuals who also lead monotonous lives as they turn to express their inner anger by beating each other senselessly. However, as the group continues to grow, soon enough, anarchy reigns.

Acclaimed filmmaker David Fincher's adaptation of Chuck Palahniuk's 1996 novel is an insightful satire of masculinity and consumerism and observes how both can be equally toxic to society. While Fincher's brilliant adaptation of Palahniuk's acclaimed novel is dark and unorthodox in many ways, the beloved '90s cult classic proved remarkably faithful to the book.

The 2007 thriller No Country for Old Men tells the story of Llewelyn Moss (Josh Brolin), who discovers the gruesome aftermath of a drug deal. Unable to resist temptation, Moss takes off with the cash left behind. However, it is not long before a tense game of cat and mouse ensues, as merciless killer Anton Chigurh (Javier Bardem) begins to pursue Moss.

The Coen brothers' adaptation of Cormac McCarthy's brilliant novel is a true masterpiece in which the filmmakers have crafted their most suspenseful and terrifying film to date. At the same time, the film adaptation has remained highly faithful to the novel regarding its primary elements, namely tone, twists, and surprises.

The cinematic masterpiece The Silence of the Lambs is an intoxicating and absorbing thriller. The film follows young FBI cadet Clarice Starling (Jodie Foster) as she seeks advice from Dr. Hannibal Lecter (Anthony Hopkins), an incarcerated cannibalistic serial killer, to track down another serial killer.

Jonathan Demme's adaptation of Thomas Harris' compelling novel The Silence of the Lambs is considered one of the most horrifying and iconic thrillers of all time. In the book-to-movie adaptation, Demme has successfully created a thrilling, thought-provoking pop-culture phenomenon close to Harris's novel in most aspects, including story and dialogue.

#3406. Three Ways to Avoid CAPTCHA Prompts When Using a VPN

VPNs make it harder to track your online activity across websites, but it also makes them suspicious about your origins. When you borrow an IP address that hundreds of other people are also using for any number of reasons, you’re much more likely to get repeat verification requests from online firewalls.

CAPTCHAs are simple puzzles that websites use to filter out bots and spam. They’re supposed to be easy for people but hard for robots, such as simple object recognition tasks or audio-visual challenges. However, they can still disrupt your browsing experience if they happen too frequently.

Most modern CAPTCHA providers, like Google's reCAPTCHA v3 or Cloudflare Turnstile, start working long before they give you a puzzle to solve. It usually starts with a risk score that studies your IP address, browser and device signals, or recent online activity.

If the CAPTCHA provider can’t confidently identify your request as human based on those signals, it requests that you complete a puzzle before deciding if the request should be blocked. That means when you get repeat CAPTCHA requests, there’s something affecting your browser’s risk score. For example, popular VPN servers spread the same IP address across any number of users, which can easily make a website mistake you for a bot farm. If you change your IP address frequently by switching servers often, that might look suspicious too.

Luckily, there are ways to deal with frequent CAPTCHA requests using tools and services available with your browser and VPN. Cloudflare has already cut its CAPTCHA requests by 91% using its Managed Challenge platform. Apple has also been shipping token-based verification on devices since iOS 16 and macOS Ventura. In June 2026, Cloudflare even announced a joint effort called the Private Access Control Tokens (PACT) standard with Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Shopify.

While there’s no direct off switch for CAPTCHAs, you can use different fixes to improve your browser’s trust signals when using the internet. That way, you’re less likely to be hounded by verification requests.

The easiest fix for repeat CAPTCHAs is to stop connecting to whichever server your VPN app picks automatically. Proton recommends choosing servers with lower traffic load. In fact, its apps display load as a percentage to help you avoid the most crowded options. I'd also skip big traffic hubs like New York or London, since that's where most traffic originates from. Servers in smaller cities located nearby are often just as fast but never as populated.

You should also avoid changing IP addresses too frequently, which can look suspicious on its own. Pick a server that seems to behave well, then continue using it for at least one session. Also remember you’re more likely to get premium server options if you’re on a paid VPN plan. Major platforms like ExpressVPN, Surfshark, Proton, and Nord are particularly likely to have a larger server collection to pick from.

Costs nothing more than your current subscription

Hopping between servers often can backfire

Private Access Tokens (PAT) let you verify the authenticity of your request using your device rather than an IP address. Apple calls it Automatic Verification, where an Apple server validates your device and Apple Account to assign you an anonymous token.

To enable Automatic Verification on an iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > [your name] > Sign-In & Security > Automatic Verification. On a Mac, open System Settings > [your name] > Sign-In & Security > Automatic Verification.

Unfortunately, there’s no equivalent feature for Windows, Android, and Linux users. That said, Cloudflare offers the Silk extension for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge that serves a similar function. A quick look at the ratings will tell you it’s not as effective, but Cloudflare’s upcoming cross-browser standard called PACT seems promising once it is released.

Doesn’t share personal details with websites

Chrome and Firefox extensions can be unreliable

If you pay a bit extra for a dedicated IP add-on, VPN providers can assign you a unique IP address that isn’t shared with anyone else. For example, NordVPN offers dedicated IPs in 30 countries for $2-5 a month and Surfshark charges $3.75 a month for it.

There are also dedicated providers like Private Internet Access, which charges $3.99 per month for a zero-trust setup so not even their employees know which IP address is assigned to you. On the other hand, Proton VPN offers dedicated IPs only to business plan users, so you’ll need to be on the Workspace Standard, Premium, or Enterprise plans to get one.

That said, there is a trade-off here too. NordVPN itself admits that a dedicated IP makes it easier to link online activity back to a single user. Also, many websites can still tell that the IP address originated from a VPN data center rather than a consumer’s device.

Get unique IP addresses with pristine reputation

Works across desktop, mobile, and even smart TVs

Also functions as an allowlisted address for work

Add-ons cost more on top of the VPN subscription

Offers less anonymity than shared VPN servers

Just yesterday I was sweating through a scorching summer night and now when I climb into bed, it’s like stepping into an igloo. Either way is bad news for my sleep and can result in 3 a.m. wake-ups. No wonder all the best mattresses we’ve tried have passed rigorous temperature regulation tests.

The best cooling mattresses use heat dissipating materials to kick out night sweats and counteract heatwaves so you’re able to snooze soundly. And when it comes to cooling beds, the Bear Elite Hybrid is the best we’ve ever tested.

But recently I’ve been hands-on with the Eight Sleep Pod 6 and Orion Sleep System, two of the best smart mattresses that use active cooling to create even temperatures. These high-tech systems deliver impressive hands-on cooling but at a high price. So in the Black Friday mattress and sleep sales, which should you buy? I'm here to advise you based on our extensive testing and my own experience with all three cooling beds.

The Eight Sleep Pod 6 is the most expensive of the three, with a queen coming in at $2,899 MSRP. The Orion is cheaper with an MSRP of $2,395. The Bear Elite Hybrid has an MSRP of $2,284 for a queen, but regular Bear mattress sales can knock it as low as $1,370.40.

Keep in mind, both the Eight Sleep Pod 6 and the Orion are covers only. The Elite Hybrid is the only option that's actually a mattress.

As well as being the priciest upfront, the Eight Sleep Pod 6 is the only one with a mandatory subscription. Starting at $17/month, it includes sleep tracking and is essential for operating the Pod. Orion also has a sleep tracking subscription but it's optional (although more expensive at $250/year). Bear, of course, is subscription-free.

Bear blows both smart covers out of the water when it comes to benefits, offering a 365-night sleep trial and a limited lifetime warranty. Orion and Eight Sleep both offer just a 30-night trial and 2-year warranty.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

With the launch of the Pod 6, Eight Sleep expanded into twin sizes, offering more options for solo sleepers. A twin is now only $1,899 (was $1,999) while there's $200 off larger sizes. Eight Sleep sales are never blockbusters so this is a noteworthy price drop, although we're hopeful more discounts will appear before Black Friday.

A queen-size smart mattress cover for under $2,000 is a rare bargain and in the Orion Black Friday sale there's up to $600 off this climate control system. Sizes are limited (just queen, king, and Cal king as of writing) but the price is fantastic. A bigger discount is unlikely, so now's the time to shop.

The Bear Elite Hybrid sells at a competitive price for a cooling hybrid mattress, particularly one with a luxury pillow-top. There's usually 30% off at Bear but keep an eye out for the 35% off deal that reliably appears over the holidays. Right now, though, you can get 40% off plus free accessories when you use our TOMS40 code at the checkout, bringing the price of a queen down to $1,370.40.

The Pod 6 and Orion Sleep System both come in two parts: the cover and a control tower. The cover is fitted with water pipes, attach to the tower via tube.

In terms of design, the tower is the primary difference between the two. The Orion tower is bigger and bulkier but also has a more design-forward finish. The Eight Sleep Pod 6 is quieter, however.

The Bear Elite Hybrid is an entirely different beast. One of the best hybrid mattresses, it's made from layers of mattress springs and foams. The cover is woven with Celliant fibers to draw away heat, while a copper-infused foam layer further aids temperature control.

The Eight Sleep Pod 6 and Orion covers are designed to make minimal difference to the support and cushioning of your mattress. I tested both on the Leesa Original mattress and, overall, I think this is accurate. That means your comfort is dependent on the mattress beneath.

As one of the best mattresses in a box you can buy, we were impressed with the support and cushioning of the Bear Elite Hybrid. It comes in three firmness levels (I tried the Medium and it's one of my favorite mattresses for side sleepers) so there's an option for nearly all sleep styles.

Dive into our Bear Elite Hybrid mattress review to learn more about the pressure relief, edge support and motion isolation of this top-rated mattress.

The Eight Sleep and Orion take a hands-on approach to temperature regulation. Both are active climate control systems, pumping water through tiny pipes in the mattress cover so the surface retains the perfect feel.

From my experience, both are highly effective. I slept on the Orion Sleep System during the change from summer to fall, meaning some days I had all the windows open, and other days I was flirting with turning the heating up. Right now, I'm using my Eight Sleep Pod 6 on some frosty nights.

Both covers keep the temperature at 'snug', staying far away from 'shivering' or 'sauna'. I haven't had a sweaty 3 a.m. wake-up in months.

Under our thermal cam, the Orion Sleep showed its prowess. It kept a steady feel the entire time, with no temperature swings even when tester Frances Daniels climbed on. And while normally a thermal outline remains long after our tester has left the mattress, on the Orion, all signs of Frances were gone in minutes.

The Bear Elite Hybrid has a more traditional approach to cooling. (Although with its Celliant fibers and copper-infused foams, it's hardly simple.)

Despite its lack of active cooling technology, our hands-on testing showed heat didn't linger in the Bear Elite. And our thermal cam backed us up. While the Bear Elite Hybrid warmed quickly, it kicked out excess heat at an incredible pace. After just four minutes of our tester leaving the mattress, it had nearly returned to the original temperature.

While the Bear Elite Hybrid is impressive, it's not as versatile as the Eight Sleep or the Orion Sleep System. And nothing touches the Eight Sleep when it comes to quick changes — buttons on the side of the cover allow you to adjust the temperature without unlocking your phone.

Orion and Eight Sleep both offer sleep tracking alongside their advanced cooling features. For Eight Sleep, the sleep tracking is part of the mandatory subscription. For Orion, it's an optional add-on.

I've tested both alongside my Oura Ring 5, our top rated sleep tracker this year. Overall, I've been impressed with the quality and accuracy of the information. Both capture sleep stages and duration that line up with both the data from my Oura Ring and my recollection of the night.

However when it comes to the details, the Eight Sleep Pod 6 is the winner. It captures a massive amount of data and displays it in easy-to-read graphics. For the Orion, sleep tracking feels like an add-on. With Eight Sleep, it's integral.

Eight Sleep also has a smart alarm built into the the cover, which vibrates when it senses a light sleep stage. Orion preps you to wake up with gentle warmth but the Eight Sleep Pod 6 does a better job at rousing you.

✅ You experience hot flashes: The Eight Sleep's hot flash mode works to quickly counteract sudden temperature fluctuations. It should kick in while you're sleeping but you can also turn it on in the app if you feel a hot flash coming on.

✅ You want detailed sleep tracking: Eight Sleep's Autopilot delivers accurate and detailed sleep data. Plus, it puts it all into handy graphics to give you an instant picture of sleep trends and changes.

✅ You want control at the touch of a button: Simply press the button on the side of the cover to turn the heat up or down in the night. The Eight Sleep isn't a mind reader, so this allows you to tweak it to fit your needs.

✅ You want smart cooling without the expense: The Orion can match the Eight Sleep (and the Bear Elite Hybrid) when it comes to temperature control, offering active cooling at a lower price.

✅ You and your partner can never agree on the thermostat: Both the Orion and Eight Sleep allow you to set a different temperature on each side of the mattress. With the Orion, you can do so for less.

✅ You need a new bed: If you go for the Orion or Eight Sleep, you'll need to buy a new mattress as well (or stick with the one you have). The Bear Elite Hybrid doesn't just offer cooling — it's a great bed all round.

✅ You don't experience major temperature swings: If you often wake up stuffy but hot sleeping isn't ruining your night, you might not require high-tech active cooling. The Bear will keep you comfortable without the expense.

#3403. Apple now sells ‘innovative’ game controller play pad and 20+ more accessories

Apple has updated its third-party accessories lineup ahead of the holidays. The refreshed lineup includes products for gaming, iPhone filmmaking, charging, and more. Among the most interesting additions is an “innovative” game controller that works with iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, Apple Vision Pro, and more.

The GAMR Active Game Controller retails for $199.95 at Apple. Apple describes it as an “innovative, pressure-sensitive game controller play pad” that lets players control compatible games by stepping and moving across nine responsive zones.

Those zones map to directional controls and the A, B, X, and Y buttons of a traditional controller. GAMR connects over Bluetooth to iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro, with support for compatible Apple Arcade and App Store games. There’s also a free GAMR app with original games.

Apple lists up to eight to ten hours of battery life, and the pad rolls up for storage between gaming sessions. Think a dance mat-style approach to playing games across Apple’s devices.

Another notable addition is the ShiftCam ProRig Filmmaker Kit, which sells for $169.95 in Titanium Silver.

The kit puts an open frame around your iPhone, with repositionable handles for shooting in landscape or portrait. A Bluetooth shutter lets you capture shots from the grip, while two cold shoe mounts and six quarter-inch mounting points provide room for lights, microphones, tripods, and other accessories.

ShiftCam also includes an adapter for compatible filters and lenses, a carrying pouch, and interchangeable bumpers for iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 18 Pro, and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

For something smaller and more affordable, Apple now sells the ShiftCam SnapPocket Light 2 Magnetic LED Ring Light for $39.95.

The pocket-sized light attaches to a MagSafe-compatible iPhone or case and flips 180 degrees to illuminate either you or your subject. It offers five brightness levels and five color temperature settings ranging from warm to cool, with a built-in battery that recharges over USB-C. ShiftCam also includes a magnetic ring sticker for attaching it to an iPad or MacBook.

The light is also included in the $159.95 ShiftCam SnapTravel Kit Pro 2, alongside a camera grip with a 5,000mAh battery and Qi2 charging, a selfie stick that converts into a tripod, and a travel pouch.

Elsewhere, Apple’s latest accessory selection includes two Belkin power banks. The $99.95 UltraCharge Pro 20K features an integrated USB-C cable with up to 70W output and two additional USB-C ports. The $49.95 BoostCharge Slim Magnetic Power Bank 5K with Stand offers 15W Qi2 wireless charging, 20W wired charging, and a built-in kickstand.

There’s also the $49.95 MOFT Snap Field MagSafe Wallet Stand, which holds up to eight cards and unfolds into a stand for your iPhone. You can also find it on Amazon.

Cases and bags round out the selection, including Tech21 FlexFolio and mophie Knit folios for iPad Air and iPad Pro, a Tech21 EvoShell for MacBook Neo, Rains sleeves, and Herschel sleeves, bags, and organizers.

You can find the complete 24-item collection here.

#3402. Rex Ryan Arrested For Allegedly Hitting 2 Pedestrians, Running Over Their Feet

Rex Ryan turned himself in to authorities Wednesday morning ... after the former NFL head coach allegedly ran over the feet of two pedestrians while driving his pickup truck in Nashville.

It's a shocking allegation against a guy who LOVES feet.

According to Nashville PD, the 63-year-old former Jets coach was driving his truck just before midnight last Thursday when he made a right turn, running over the feet of two people who were crossing the street.

The alleged victims told police Ryan kept driving, but they managed to catch up to him at a red light ... where a heated argument kicked off, with Rex even getting out of his vehicle.

After exchanging words, the pedestrians told cops Ryan bolted without exchanging information ... but they were able to snap a photo of his license plate.

The pedestrians went to the authorities, and a warrant was issued for Rex's arrest. The charges ... two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failing to give information/render aid, and two counts of failing to obey traffic signals.

The whole incident is ironic, if nothing else.

Back in 2010, Deadspin published videos of Ryan rubbing a woman's feet, and the jokes always been, the dude loves feet.

#3401. JBL's Latest Portable Party Speaker Is $150 Off in This Early Black Friday Deal

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

Woot has dropped the price of the JBL PartyBox 330 to $479.95 as an early Black Friday deal, saving you $150 and bringing it to its lowest price to date, according to price trackers. For comparison, the same speaker currently costs $629.95 at Amazon, although that purchase includes a 90-day free trial of Amazon Music. Woot, meanwhile, offers free shipping for Prime members ($6 otherwise), and covers the new unit with a 90-day limited warranty.

Beyond the discount, the PartyBox 330 has plenty to offer if you're looking for a speaker that can handle everything from backyard barbecues to larger gatherings—sitting between the smaller Club 120 and the larger PartyBox 520 in JBL's lineup, it delivers deep, punchy bass and enough volume to entertain a crowd, while its roughly 20-hour battery life means you can keep the music going all day without having to find an outlet. It's also rated IPX4 for water resistance, so a little rain or an accidental splash shouldn't be a problem.

That protection has limits, though—the 330 isn’t dustproof or particularly impact-resistant, so you’ll still want to be careful where you set it down. Audio-wise, sound quality also changes depending on where you're standing, with music becoming noticeably more muffled from the sides and behind. Fortunately, JBL's graphic equalizer and sound presets give you some control over the tuning. Its two microphone inputs and a guitar input also make it suitable for karaoke nights or live performances. You also get Bluetooth, USB-C audio, and an optical input for connecting it to a TV, along with Auracast support if you want to link it with other compatible JBL speakers for a larger setup.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, but prices aren’t always what they seem. Use a price tracker to make sure you’re getting the best deal, or refer to guides like our live blog that use price trackers for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

#3400. Taika Waititi’s Next Film Officially Shelved Following Controversy

Editor's Note: The following contains descriptions of sexual misconduct that some readers may find disturbing.

It has not been a great time for Taika Waititi? It feels like everything the New Zealander touches these days is cursed, and his newest project is no exception. One of his next appearances was supposed to be in a family-friendly fantasy movie adapted from a popular children's book, with a cast that included several familiar faces. Unfortunately, the production has now found itself caught up in a controversy unrelated to its leading man, and its release plans have taken a significant hit.

Waititi's upcoming fantasy film Fing! has officially lost its UK and Ireland distributor, with Sky confirming that it intends to withdraw from the project following serious allegations against author and screenwriter David Walliams. The decision comes after a joint investigation by The Guardian and ITV News reported allegations of inappropriate behavior involving teenage girls and young women.

The film, which stars Waititi alongside Mia Wasikowska and Iona Bell, is based on Walliams' bestselling children's novel. Walliams also co-wrote the screenplay and had filmed a cameo appearance, but the producers have now confirmed that his scene has been removed and that he will have no involvement in promoting or releasing the movie. In a statement to Variety, the producers explained:

"We take the allegations reported regarding David Walliams seriously. Our thoughts are with anyone who has been affected. We have removed his cameo appearance from Fing!, and he will have no involvement in the film’s release or promotion."

Sky, which was set to release the film as one of its originals, has also announced its intention to abandon its distribution agreement. A spokesperson said:

"The allegations made against David Walliams are extremely serious. We have notified the producers of the film of our intention to exit our position as the U.K. & Ireland licensee of Fing."

Walliams, who is a well-established British entertainment figure thanks to his work as a children's author as well as the co-creator and star of Little Britain, and as a judge on Britain's Got Talent, has just lost a long, and heavily publicized legal battle to prevent his name from being published by the English and Welsh press in relation to sexual misconduct. #3399. Apple Music launches ‘Best of 2026’ content, reveals Artist of the Year

Apple Music has launched new playlists and curated content for the ‘Best of 2026’ and also revealed its new Artist of the Year.

The year is coming to a close, and Apple Music’s editorial teams have published a variety of playlists and other content to wrap the year.

Inside the ‘New’ tab in Apple Music, you’ll find ‘Best of 2026’ versions of popular playlists like Rap Life, R&B Now, A-List Pop, Today’s Country, and more.

Additionally, Apple Music has named its Artist of the Year for 2026: Olivia Dean

Olivia Dean was announced today as Apple Music’s Artist of the Year, recognizing her undeniable leap to stardom in what’s been the defining feel-good music story of 2026. She is the first UK artist to receive this honor.

Olivia’s late 2025 album, The Art of Loving, truly broke through this year. Her hit “Man I Need” has charted on Apple Music’s Daily Top 100 every day since first appearing on August 29, 2025. In addition to selling out her global tour, she won a GRAMMY for Best New Artist and four BRIT Awards, including Artist of the Year. In fall 2025, Olivia opened for Sabrina Carpenter at Madison Square Garden, in New York City. Less than a year later, she returned for her own four-night residency and followed up with a six-night sold-out run at The O2 Arena, in London.

Like Apple has done for the last several years, it’s gifting Dean with a physical that includes a custom Apple silicon wafer “suspended between a polished sheet of glass, and a machined and anodized aluminum body.”

Last year’s Artist of the Year was Tyler, The Creator, in 2024 it was Billie Eilish, and in 2023 Taylor Swift won the prize.

Apple Music is available for $11.99/month, or you can get it as part of the Apple One bundle.
